meta.title: MKWMP: play Mario Kart World online on your PC
meta.description: MKWMP sets up mkw-recomp from your own copy of the game, plays offline right away, and takes you online to community servers with friends, voice chat and mods. Free and open source.
meta.host_title: Host an MKWMP server: a cloud VM in one command
meta.host_description: Run your own MKWMP server on a small Vultr VM: SSH keys, the firewall, one command, HTTPS, updates and backups.

hero.title: Race online. On your terms.
hero.lead: MKWMP is a launcher for mkw-recomp, the PC version of Mario Kart World built from your own copy of the game. It sets the game up for you, plays offline as soon as it's ready, and takes you online to community servers, with friends, voice chat and mods.
hero.shot_alt: The MKWMP launcher's Home: Play Online, Friends, Game and What's New tiles, and the dock below.

upgrade.title: Coming from 1.3?
upgrade.text: 1.4 is a new launcher (mkwmp.exe), and 1.3 can't update itself to it. Download 1.4 once, by hand, and unzip it into the same folder as your 1.3: it keeps your gamertag, PIN, server and choices. Then delete the old mkwmp-launcher.exe. On a Steam Deck, the command below does all of this.

setup.title: Set up in one go
setup.lead: Point MKWMP at your own copy of the game, version 1.8.0, as a .nup, an .nx or a folder. It does the rest.
setup.s1c: MKWMP's build, 0.1.16-mkwmp.1, checked against its known hash. On a CPU without AVX2 it picks the build made for it.
setup.s2c: It reads your copy where it is, or copies it, as you choose. Nothing of the game is downloaded.
setup.s3c: mkw-recomp's own setup: generate, compile (about 4 minutes), shaders (10 to 16 minutes on a Steam Deck), warm-up and clean-up.
setup.s4c: Online play, friends and the in-game overlay, inside the game.
setup.s5c: Everything lives next to the launcher, nothing in AppData. Settings › Game switches to another copy of the game later.
setup.shot_alt: The game setup in progress: a progress bar, the current step and the time left.
setup.shot_cap: The first setup takes a while. After that the game starts in seconds.

offline.title: Offline first, online when you want
offline.lead: Once the game is set up, it's yours to play, with no account. Going online is one choice away: pick a server, register a gamertag, get a PIN.
offline.r2c: Pick a server from the list, or type the address a host gave you.
offline.r3c: Your gamertag, friends and PIN live on the server you choose. The PIN signs you in on another PC or a Steam Deck.
offline.r4c: The launcher updates itself and the MKWMP mod. What's New shows what changed.
offline.shot_alt: The launcher asking "Want to go online?" with Play Offline and Go Online.

servers.title: Servers
servers.lead: Anyone can host a server. Public ones list themselves in the server directory, and the launcher shows them nearest first. This list is live.
servers.note: Your browser can only time servers that use HTTPS; the launcher times every one. Lower is better: green under 80 ms, yellow under 160 ms.
servers.noscript: The live list needs JavaScript. The launcher shows the same list.
servers.shot_alt: The launcher's Choose a Server screen: servers with latency bars, seats and queue.
servers.shot_cap: The same list in the launcher, where every server is timed.

friends.title: Friends, voice and camera
friends.lead: Add friends by gamertag and see who's playing. Voice chat and the camera work only in private friend rooms, never with strangers in matchmaking.
friends.r1c: Requests, who's online and who's racing, and their rooms to join.
friends.r2c: In friend rooms, for everyone in the room. Mute anyone. Relayed live and never recorded.
friends.r3c: Off until you turn it on. Only mutual friends in your room see it, up to 4 faces each.
friends.r4c: Report voice or camera abuse from the launcher. The server's host reviews it.
friends.shot_alt: Home with the friends panel open: requests and friends with their status.

overlay.title: The in-game overlay
overlay.lead: In the game, press Guide (Home) or Select + Start. The game pauses and shrinks into the launcher's Home, with your friends, settings and Quit game right there.
overlay.r1c: B or Guide returns to the game where you left it.
overlay.r2c: See who's online and answer requests from the overlay.
overlay.note: The overlay needs mkw-recomp 0.1.16-mkwmp(.1) with the MKWMP mod: the launcher sets up both.
overlay.shot_alt: The overlay: the paused game shrunk into the Home screen's Play tile.

mods.title: Mods
mods.lead: Browse GameBanana from the launcher, install with one button, and switch mods on and off.
mods.r1c: Search and sort GameBanana. Previews of mature mods stay blurred unless you choose otherwise.
mods.r2: From a link or a file
mods.r2c: Install a .zip, .7z or .rar from a link or from your disk.
mods.r3c: Mods that ship options get their own page in the launcher.
mods.r4c: Mods that run their own code ask first. Mods that change the game's code stay on mkw-recomp's own Mods page. Every player's save is backed up before playing with a new set of mods.
mods.shot_alt: Get Mods: a grid of GameBanana mods with search and sorting.

langs.title: 15 languages, light and dark
langs.lead: The launcher follows your system's language and theme, or the ones you pick.
langs.section: Made for the couch and the desk
langs.r1c: Every screen works with a controller, like a console menu, and with a keyboard or a mouse.
langs.r2c: The same look in both. This site switches too (the button at the top, or Y on a controller).
langs.r3c: On a TV, a monitor or a Steam Deck.
langs.shot_alt: Settings, Appearance: theme, full screen and language.

deck.title: Steam Deck and SteamOS
deck.lead: One command in Desktop Mode (Konsole) installs MKWMP, adds it to Steam with artwork and the controller layout, and runs it under Proton.
deck.r1c: The installer edits Steam's shortcuts, which needs Steam closed.
deck.r2c: ~/Games/MKWMP, with a Steam shortcut called MKWMP that runs under Proton 11.
deck.r3c: It brings over the 1.3 launcher's settings and removes the old MKWMP shortcuts.
deck.r4c: --dir, --proton, --dry-run and --uninstall, among others. Add them after bash -s --.
deck.shot_alt: The launcher's Home on a Steam Deck.

host.title: Host your own server
host.lead: A small cloud VM, about US$5 a month, runs a server for dozens of players. One command installs it, opens the firewall and lists it in the server directory, so it shows up in everyone's launcher.
host.r1c: Vultr, Ubuntu 24.04, one command. Optional HTTPS with your domain.
host.r2c: server.exe from the server download, double-click: for friends or a LAN party.
host.r3c: The full hosting guide on GitHub.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: Each server has its own privacy policy. The launcher shows it after you sign in, and the server records which version you accepted. When the policy changes, you're asked again.
privacy.r1c: The launcher asks before it signs you in or plays online.
privacy.r2c: Your gamertag, a hash of your PIN (never the PIN), your friends, the policy you accepted and the reports you file. No email and no real name.
privacy.r3c: They're relayed live inside friend rooms, never stored.
privacy.r4c: From the launcher, at any time.
privacy.note: Shown live from mkw.anarqz.dev/privacy. Other servers have their own.
privacy.shot_alt: Before you play online: the 18+ confirmation and the server's privacy policy.

faq.title: Questions
faq.a1: No. It's a fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. It doesn't use Nintendo's servers.
faq.a2: Yes: your own copy of the game, version 1.8.0. MKWMP never downloads the game; it builds mkw-recomp from your copy.
faq.a3: On the Steam Deck and SteamOS, through Proton: use the command above. Other Linux desktops with Steam and Proton work the same way.
faq.a4: Yes. MKWMP is open source (GPL-3.0). Servers are run by their hosts; the official one is free to play on.
faq.q5: I'm on 1.3. How do I update?
faq.a5: Download 1.4 by hand once and unzip it into your 1.3 folder: 1.3 can't update itself to the new launcher. Your gamertag, PIN and server carry over. Then delete the old mkwmp-launcher.exe. On a Steam Deck, run the install command: it brings your 1.3 settings over.
faq.q6: The game crashed. Where do I report it?
faq.a6: The launcher shows a crash report after a crash: it saves a zip on your Desktop (no PIN or keys in it) and opens a new GitHub issue with the details filled in. "Found a bug?" in the launcher does the same any time.

hostpage.title: Host an MKWMP server
hostpage.lead: A Vultr VM and one command. About US$5 a month runs a server for dozens of players. You need a Vultr account, an SSH key, and a few minutes.
hostpage.ssh_text: You log in to the VM with a key, not a password. If you don't have one, create it on your own computer (PowerShell on Windows, a terminal on macOS or Linux) and press Enter at each question:
hostpage.ssh_after: Your public key is now in ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub (on Windows, C:\Users\<you>\.ssh\id_ed25519.pub). Add it at Vultr: Account → SSH Keys → Add SSH Key. Never share id_ed25519 without .pub: that's the private half.
hostpage.vm_text: Pick a region close to most of your players: the relay and the voice and camera relay run on this VM. When it's running, note its public IPv4 address.
hostpage.vm_size_v: 1 vCPU, 1 GB RAM, about US$5 a month
hostpage.fw_text: Vultr filters traffic before it reaches the VM. Create a firewall group with these inbound rules and attach it to the VM. The script opens the same ports inside the VM (ufw), so the two layers agree. Leave outbound traffic open.
hostpage.fw_seat: the seat API: the launcher signs in and takes a seat (80 and 443 instead with a domain)
hostpage.fw_turn: the TURN relay, for players who can't reach each other directly
hostpage.fw_voice: voice chat and camera relay (friend rooms)
hostpage.fw_how: In Vultr: Network → Firewall → Add Firewall Group, add the rules, then add your VM on the group's Linked Instances tab.
hostpage.run_text: Log in and run it as root:
hostpage.run_does: It asks for the server's name and region, then:
hostpage.run_1: downloads the server from the latest MKWMP release and checks it against the release's signed checksums, with the MKWMP release key built into the script (it stops if anything doesn't match);
hostpage.run_2: creates the mkwmp user and /var/lib/mkwmp: keys, the gamertag database, the config and your privacy policy;
hostpage.run_3: installs two services, mkwmp-seat for launchers and mkwmp-lobby for the game, and keeps their logs for 7 days;
hostpage.run_4: opens the ports in ufw, keeping SSH open;
hostpage.run_5: lists the server in the server directory, so it shows up in everyone's launcher;
hostpage.run_6: checks that it answers from outside and that the directory lists it, then prints the address players use.
hostpage.opt_name: the name in the launcher and the server list: up to 32 letters, digits, spaces and _ . -
hostpage.opt_region: a short tag for the server list, like sa-east, us-east or eu-west
hostpage.opt_capacity: players seated at once (50 by default); the rest wait in a queue
hostpage.opt_publicip: the address players reach the VM at, if it isn't the VM's own
hostpage.opt_noannounce: stay out of the public server list; players type your address
hostpage.opt_uninstall: remove the services, the program and the ufw rules; keeps /var/lib/mkwmp (add --purge to delete it too)
hostpage.policy_text: Players see /var/lib/mkwmp/privacy.md in the launcher and accept it. The script writes a template the first time: edit it so it's true for your server (who you are, how to reach you, how long you keep logs), then run systemctl restart mkwmp-seat. Every edit is a new version, and players are asked to accept it again.
hostpage.https_text: Over plain http://, PINs travel unencrypted. With a domain:
hostpage.https_1: Create a DNS A record, like mkw.example.net, pointing at the VM's public IPv4. At Cloudflare, make it DNS only (grey cloud) at first, so the certificate can be issued.
hostpage.https_2: In the cloud firewall, open TCP 80 and 443 (you can close 7000).
hostpage.https_3: Run the script again with --domain mkw.example.net. It installs Caddy, which gets and renews a Let's Encrypt certificate, keeps the seat API on the VM only, and lists https://mkw.example.net in the directory.
hostpage.https_after: The game's own ports (8905, 8906 and the UDP ones) still go straight to the VM's IP address.
hostpage.ops_update_t: Run the script again. It remembers its options, installs the latest release and keeps gamertags, friends and keys. Restarting the lobby doesn't end running games.
hostpage.ops_backup_t: /var/lib/mkwmp is everything: registry.db (gamertags, PIN hashes, friends) and keys/ (your server's identity). Stop mkwmp-seat, archive the folder, start it again. Keep backups private and delete old ones: they hold your players' data.
hostpage.ops_admin_t: Gamertags and reports: sudo -u mkwmp /opt/mkwmp/bin/server admin list --config /var/lib/mkwmp/server.toml, and the other admin commands in the hosting guide.
hostpage.tr_1: The script stops at "signature does NOT verify"
hostpage.tr_1c: The download was altered or cut short. Run it again; don't install by hand.
hostpage.tr_2: "/ping did not answer from this VM"
hostpage.tr_2c: The cloud firewall isn't attached or lacks TCP 7000 (or 80 and 443 with a domain). With --domain, the A record may not point at the VM yet.
hostpage.tr_3c: journalctl -u mkwmp-seat | grep announce. "HTTP 400 … endpoint" means a private address (use --public-ip); "connect" means outbound HTTPS is blocked.
hostpage.tr_4: Launchers connect, but the game can't
hostpage.tr_4c: TCP 8905 and 8906 closed in the cloud firewall; systemctl status mkwmp-lobby.
hostpage.tr_5: Players can't race or talk together
hostpage.tr_5c: The UDP ports (3478, 49152–49407, 8907, 10025) closed in the cloud firewall.
hostpage.pc_text: For friends or a LAN party, download the server zip from the latest release and run server.exe (Windows) or ./server (Linux). The first run asks for the address players reach your PC at, creates mkwmp-data next to it, and runs until you close it. Over the internet, forward the ports above on your router. Players set the launcher's server to http://<that address>:7000.
hostpage.more: Docker, a by-hand systemd setup and every option: the full hosting guide on GitHub.
